brief: What began in October as a rotation out of extended Tech has morphed into a wider rout via the US mid-term blue wave, concerns around NVDA, fears of heavy equity supply, and concurrent tech outages, leaving the S&P 500 down more than 10% from its peak. DB frames 10% pullbacks as rare (about once a year) versus routine 3-5% dips tied to clear shocks. Aggregate equity positioning has fallen to -0.9sd (11th percentile), now low even in absolute terms and not just relative to earnings growth, with both discretionary (4th/5th percentile) and systematic (15th/16th percentile, biggest underweight in 18 months) strategies cutting sharply. Pricing and positioning now sit in line with an outright S&P 500 earnings contraction and sub-50 PMIs, about halfway to the median -24% post-war recession decline. Vol, intraday ranges, the VIX curve inversion and stock correlations spiked into the top decile, which DB calls a vol shock (>1.5sd), historically taking 6-8 weeks to subside with -14% to -16% further declines outside recessions. Tech sits at the bottom of its decade-long channel both absolutely and relative to the market, with the Nasdaq 100 over 10% below its 200dma, only the 5th such instance in a decade. Weekly equity fund inflows ($66.6bn) stayed robust while bonds saw their first outflows since Liberation Day.
